releases.notes:
- **A phone-friendly RepoOS in the browser.** Below 720px wide, RepoOS now serves a layout built for phones: a bottom tab bar (Work, Search, More, Settings) with a More sheet, a single-column Work queue with a New task button, status filter and sort, a task detail page, and a mobile Settings view. Desktop is unchanged, and the same layout works in a phone browser, as a home-screen app and inside the native shell. The design is recorded in ADR 0011 (#1110, #1112, #1113, #1114, #1115).
- **Move to done works again from the task drawer.** Since the "Land anyway" option arrived, the drawer's Move to done button was refused instantly with "Land anyway requires a reason of 1–1000 characters". Clicking it from the board card was never affected. The drawer button now works, with regression tests (hotfix on main).
- **Stuck tasks recover on their own.** A failed review pass is retried automatically, and when a message to an engineer sits undelivered with no engineer running, the engineer is restarted (#1108).
- **`repoos restart` handles a hand-started server,** or says clearly why it cannot (#1109).
- **Faster, steadier checks.** The full check's tests step is about 20% faster, and several tests that failed only under load or on a remote host were fixed: `remote-host-pool` on the remote check host, `check-skip-outcome` and `engineer-resources` (#1117, #1118, #1107).
- **Docs and the landing page match the last release.** User docs, the docs site and the llms files were checked against the new commands and screens (#1111).
releases.knownIssues:
- On a phone, the floating head icons still reserve a side column and the touch fixes for Releases and Activity are not finished; both are in progress (#1116).
- If a task drawer was already open before the upgrade, reload the page so the fixed Move to done button is used.

releases.notes:
- **Landing after a merge-conflict fix is faster.** When a conflict is resolved by taking main's side only, a "Keep review verdict and merge" button on the failed close-out card and the Debug tab (and `repoos review keep <id>`) re-pins the review to the new branch tip and merges, instead of waiting for a full re-review (#1103).
- **See every RepoOS server on your tailnet.** `repoos servers --tailscale` lists the servers on this machine and on each reachable Tailscale peer in one table with a host column; unreachable hosts are shown as such and never fail the command (#1105).
- **The restart notice is a proper dialog.** It now uses the shared dialog styling, offers a "Copy restart command" button on servers that are not supervised instead of dead buttons, and no longer announces a version while a release is still being cut. In the "newer release available" dialog, only the release notes scroll when they are long, and the notes keep list spacing (#1104).
- **Releases are more reliable.** A push of main that actually succeeded is no longer reported as a failure, a retry after a pushed main resumes at tagging without re-running the full check, host and git errors on remote validation are labelled as host failures instead of test failures, and a guard flags tests that hardcode the current version number (#1106).
releases.knownIssues: - Some load-related test flakes can still fail a full release check; rerun the release if one does.

releases.notes:
- **Reviews converge on their own.** The reviewer now ends each bug list with a single "no further findings of this class" line, leftover non-blocking suggestions can be filed as a follow-up task in one click, the review panel shows "round N of ~4" with a per-task convergence history, and you can land a task anyway with a recorded reason when its checks pass (#1081). A review that says "None found" and then explains its checks no longer counts as listing blocking bugs (#1097).
- **You can see why an agent failed.** Expired sign-in, an unavailable model or a missing CLI now shows a plain-language reason on the task card and in a notification, with the raw CLI error one click away (#1098). The default Copilot model no longer fails, and tier errors are explained (#1088).
- **Release emails.** Any project with email configured can email its team when a release is published, with richer templates, a send-to-self test and a `repoos release email --preview <version>` command (#1071, #1094, #1093, #1092).
- **Upgrades are easier to notice and apply.** The CLI and dashboard tell you when a newer RepoOS release exists (#1072), say when an installed upgrade is waiting for a restart and offer Restart now (#1075), and `repoos restart` restarts the server whether hand-run, supervised or a managed service (#1091).
- **The server is harder to knock over.** An EPERM from `kill()` no longer crashes the server (#1079), remote validation lock waiters time out instead of leaking (#1099), the Linux service install keeps PATH so agent CLIs launch (#1100), and Docker/ssh failure handling on remote capture is more complete (#1068).
- **Guardrails for landing.** WIP checkpoints and branch diffs refuse huge or build-output files (#1096), source changes committed then reverted during a check are caught (#1077), and human-assigned tasks require a step-by-step guide (#1074).
- **Smaller fixes.** Drawer status cards show one at a time with fixed spacing (#1084), the Releases page no longer blames an unrelated failed workflow (#1090), a release in progress shows the activity animation (#1089), the card last-activity popover works on touch (#1069), per-view skeletons use the show-delay gate (#1078), the handoff waiting label shows in the drawer (#1087), and `isPreviewProcess` is stricter about orphaned custom commands (#0363).
- **Flaky tests fixed.** The jsdom "Element is not defined" teardown failure (#1102) and a remote-host-pool queue test that failed under load (#1101) no longer fail unrelated tasks' checks.
releases.knownIssues: - Keeping a review verdict after a take-main's-side merge-conflict fix is not built yet; the task needs a fresh review after the merge (#1103).

releases.notes:
## Highlights

- **Stuck "checks running" labels are gone.** A handoff record that outlived its check is now cleared or marked stale, so the task card, drawer and CLI show the real state and Move to done is no longer disabled by a leftover record. Checkpoint recovery after Move to done is now single-flight, and a pending delta review is no longer lost on a restart (#1085).
- **A stale "a review is already running" marker no longer blocks reviews.** Every path that can end a review now clears its registration, a stale one is reaped, and board reads no longer do process probing for idle tasks (#1083).
- **Task branches stop failing the scope check on bookkeeping that main legitimately has.** Handoff and sync restore or drop other tasks' work files so a branch only contains its own files, even when other tasks landed while it was open (#1086).
- **Pipeline cards use the same activity animation as Board cards,** and animations pause when not visible (#1062).

## Known issues

- Remaining edge cases of the stale-record and review-marker fixes are tracked as follow-ups (#1087 and the notes in #1083 and #1085).
- The shell swaps the loading skeleton for the page instantly; a smooth fade is planned (#1078).

## Highlights

- **Reviews converge in fewer rounds.** After a set number of passes the reviewer now treats leftover edge cases as suggestions instead of blockers, task types like Easter-egg bundles and p3 tasks get a lighter bar from pass 1, and an "Accepted scope" section in a task is honoured by the reviewer (#1080).
- **Handoffs wait for a running check instead of failing.** A handoff that arrives while the engineer's own check is still running now waits (bounded) instead of failing with "A check is running" (#1082).
- **Task branches no longer pick up other tasks' bookkeeping.** The engineer self-check commit only stages the task's own files, and handoff restores any other task's work files from main, so tasks stop failing landing with "the diff changes another task's bookkeeping" (#1076).
- **The release update dialog now shows how to upgrade.** It shows the right command for how RepoOS was installed (standalone, package manager, source checkout or a beta channel) with a Copy button, and remembers a dismissed version (#1073).
- **First-load skeletons match each page's real layout** on Mission Control and Stories, with no stray second row (#1070).

## Known issues

- A stale "a review is already running" marker can still block a review until the server restarts; fix in progress (#1083).
- A handoff record can stay at "running" after the work has moved on, and the card shows "checks running" (#1085).
- A task branch can still fail the scope check on bookkeeping that main legitimately has when another task landed while it was open (#1086).
- The shell now swaps the loading skeleton for the page instantly; a smooth fade is planned (#1078).

## Highlights

- **Checks are no longer invalidated by RepoOS's own bookkeeping commits.** While a task's check runs, RepoOS now holds a short-lived check lock: its own bookkeeping commits wait until the check finishes, new engineer turns are refused, and any real source change that lands during a check is detected and fails the check with the commit and paths named. This removes a major source of "the worktree changed while the check ran" handoff failures (#1061).
- **Calmer task cards.** A healthy running card no longer shows "active just now / N minutes ago"; the last-activity time appears in a popover on hover and keyboard focus. Silent and stuck cards still show their recency (#1058).

## Known issues

- Source edits made by an already-running engineer during a check are detected after the fact, not blocked, and git submodules or nested repositories are not covered by that detection. A source change that is committed and then reverted within the same check window is not caught yet (follow-up #1077).
- Hover details on cards are mouse and keyboard only; touch support is planned as part of the mobile work (#1069).
- A handoff that arrives while the engineer's own check is still running can fail with "A check is running" instead of waiting; fix in progress (#1082).
- Remaining Docker/ssh failure-handling edge cases in remote validation are tracked in #1068.

## Highlights

- **Remote browser captures no longer stall.** The runner now exits as soon as a capture finishes, finished captures are collected and cleaned up automatically, and a failed handoff cancels its own outstanding captures. This removes the 15-30 minute waits and the pile-up of stale capture containers that slowed every task's handoff (#1060).
- **Faster checks for bookkeeping-only changes.** When a diff only touches task bookkeeping or docs, the check skips the full test suite (#1059).

## Improvements and fixes

- Review card no longer says "ready to finish" while checks are still running or failing (#1065).
- Pipeline view: card text uses a readable colour in every theme (#1066).
- Muse usage row: clearer messages and a better dashboard link (#1067).

## Known issues

- Cancelling remote captures is verified on the Tailscale runner. Parity for the other remote provider (for example Hetzner) and a few rarer Docker/ssh failure-handling edge cases are tracked in #1068.
- Two further items are still in review and are not in this release: bookkeeping commits invalidating a running check (#1061) and hover-only "last active" details on cards (#1058).

### Reviewed work now lands on repos with no remote

Move to done failed with "could not get main SHA" on a local-only repo when the machine's git `init.defaultBranch` named a branch that didn't exist (for example `master` on a repo whose branch is `main`). RepoOS now only trusts a default branch that really exists, and falls back to `main`, then `master`, then the branch that is checked out. If it still can't read the branch, the error now says which branch it tried and why.

### Review reports no longer appear as Inbox tasks

While the server was running, each review report written under `work/reports/` could show up on the board as a task named `review-1`, `review-2` and so on. Reports are now ignored by the live board the same way they are on startup.

### Clearer task cards and a faster board

- Cards and the task panel show running checks with a single status line and a live progress bar. The old fake progress bar is gone.
- A task no longer shows PAUSED during handoff, and a deferred handoff now wakes the engineer.
- The Done column loads lazily and starts collapsed, so boards with many finished tasks open faster.
- Pipeline cards show the review round and a "sent back" note.
- There is a simplified client project board for sharing progress.

### Smarter project work

- When a task lands, the PM agent now writes a summary report of what changed.
- Human tasks have a Mark done dialog with a multi-line completion report.
- Diff highlighting follows your active theme pair.
- Muse appears on the Model providers tab, with a row of provider shortcuts at the top.

### Fixes

- Task ids from 1000 up are no longer dropped from `depends_on`.
- `repoos message` and send-back accept stdin, files and heredocs, and never send junk as a message.
- Remote validation no longer kills healthy runs as hung, keeps its evidence, and cleans up leaked containers.

### Known issue

On the Work Pipeline view, the task id, type chips, elapsed time and model line on each card are hard to read in every theme. The next release fixes this.

### More reliable Muse engineering runs

Muse engineers can now run with a higher step limit, clearer notice when that limit is reached, and smoother handling of streamed output. They’re also guided to scope screenshot selectors to the relevant fixture card.

### Expanded Muse model support

The available Muse models now include Spark 1.3, Spark 1.2, and Wonder 1.0. Native Muse drivers for Spark 1.3 and Contributor can also be included in the budget allowlist.

### A Pipeline view for work in flight

The Work page has a new **Pipeline** view alongside the board. Each active or review task gets its own lane and moves through **Coding → Checks → Handoff → Review → Close-out → Merged**, so you can see at a glance where everything stands, including rounds, models, and whether a task ran locally or on a remote runner. Recently merged tasks stay in the Merged column for a short window, tasks sent back from review carry an amber “sent back” note, and stuck, held, or paused tasks keep their stage with a clear state chip. Stages update live, clicking a card opens the usual task panel, and the view remembers your choice. The board remains the default.

### Installs and uninstalls now match reality

- The curl installer puts the program in `~/.local/share/repoos` and keeps machine state in `~/.repoos`, so reinstalling no longer wipes running-server and check-slot state.
- `repoos uninstall` removes what it owns and tells you exactly what it left behind; per-repo configuration and caches are untouched.
- The installer now enforces Node **20.6.0+**, not just “Node 20”, and the docs explain the Bun/pnpm `PATH` setup steps.
- mise is no longer presented as a recommended install method; its download threshold and minimum release age made it install the previous version.
- The Homebrew formula’s Node dependency is now documented rather than left as a surprise, and install examples consistently use `curl … | bash`.

### Clearer task and agent state

- Close-out progress in the task panel now appears as a full-width status line between the preview row and the tabs. It no longer looks like a button or pushes **Stop MTD** onto its own row.
- `repoos driver brief` and the CTO no longer call an engineer “stalled” while its check is running with a live heartbeat, so a healthy check cannot be interrupted by a restart.
- PM-added sections such as Problem, Desired UX, and Acceptance criteria now land above the original freeform prompt and screenshots instead of being buried below them.
- The macOS Hub CI job no longer fails on every run because of a keyboard-focus test that could not hold focus on a headless runner.

### Interface polish

- The **Hold task** dialog uses the same outlined fields as the rest of the app, allows holding without a reason, and the held card handles a missing reason without a blank row or cramped padding.
- **New schedule**, **New reminder**, and **New environment** now match **New task**: accent style, plus icon, and top-right placement.
- The task-card agent popover fades out after 15 seconds by default; the delay is configurable in Settings, `0` disables it, and interacting with the popover resets the timer.
- The optional commit-message field in the Uncommitted changes panel is about three lines tall instead of filling most of the panel.

### Smoother setup and CLI

- `repoos init` templates no longer reference paths that do not exist in a new project, so `repoos doctor` starts clean.
- The `serve` banner states which interfaces are bound, and the docs explain Tailscale detection and how to force localhost with `--host 127.0.0.1`.
- Zero-commit repositories and Git identity supplied through environment variables are handled correctly by `repoos status`, `repoos new`, and `repoos init --new`; auto-committing on `new` is now documented.
- `repoos list` prints one short notice instead of a long warning when no server is running.
- Saving a schedule warns when its task template is missing Problem, Acceptance criteria, or Notes for AI — advisory, with a badge on the schedule card and the same warning from `repoos schedule new` and `update`.
- CLI docs now cover `repoos uninstall`, `repoos service`, and `--version`, and several messages point to the right docs and describe the runtime accurately.

The web app no longer eats your CPU while idle, and engineer agents survive server restarts

**Top priority in this release was making RepoOS cheaper to run and less likely to stall your work in flight.**

### A quieter web app
An open dashboard used to burn 30–97% of a CPU after a day or two in a tab or PWA window, loaded the server, and in bad cases dragged whole-machine load up with it. Idle work in the renderer has been found and fixed: when nothing is changing, an open board costs essentially nothing. When the tab is hidden, polling and animations pause. Memory stays bounded over long sessions.

### Engineers survive server restarts
An engineer agent that was mid-task when the server restarted used to silently go idle afterward — it looked alive to the new server process, but queued messages were never delivered and no progress was made until someone stopped and started it by hand. Restarting the server mid-task no longer needs your intervention: an adopted engineer that can't communicate is now detected and restarted automatically, and queued messages get delivered instead of sitting overdue for an hour.

### Smoother closing out tasks
- **Move to done no longer fails for bookkeeping churn.** Previously, publishing a finished task could abort **after the entire validation gate** (which can take 10–25 minutes) just because other live tasks' task files were momentarily dirty on `main` — a routine state when several engineers are running. That no longer blocks the merge; genuinely dirty source files and repo settings still do.
- **Review timeouts are now fair.** Reviews were cut off at a hard-coded 15 minutes, so large diffs on slower models died mid-review with a confusing "no usable report," ate a review round, and needed a manual retry. The timeout is now configurable in Settings, a timeout is reported as a timeout (not a missing report), and one automatic retry happens before your attention is asked for.
- **Engineering reports count only your words.** The 1,000-word cap used to include the server-generated change summary and file list, so a task touching many files got rejected at handoff even with a short report. The cap now applies to the engineer's own narrative only (soft target ~1,000, hard cap 1,200 words), regardless of diff size.

### Project history that outlives your machine
- **Review reports are now committed to the repo**, side by side with engineering rounds under `work/reports/<task-id>/`. Previously they lived in a local, gitignored cache and vanished with it — leaving no record of why a task passed through several review rounds. Existing reports were migrated and old locations still read.
- **Worktree cleanup is safer and explains itself.** Clean worktrees for merged tasks are now reclaimed automatically at boot and close-out, instead of piling up until a manual `repoos gc`. `repoos gc --dry-run` and status distinguish safe candidates from entries kept for a stated reason (unmerged commits, dirty source, active or human-owned work — all preserved), and outside-RepoOS worktrees are never touched.

### Fixes and smaller improvements
- Stray test helper processes no longer accumulate for days, adding memory pressure and stalling checks. Test runs kill everything they spawn on teardown, and a background reaper (every 10–15 minutes, never matching by process name, never touching live work) cleans stragglers that slip through.
- The "Cancel stalled check" button on a task no longer flickers on and off every few seconds while a check is progressing.
- In the task drawer, the Review and Engineer report tables no longer let the selected row's accent bar cover the pass number, and the Dev tab now uses the same layout and styling as the Review tab (Report on the left, Chat on the right, with the model selector always visible above).
